correctness.rationale: For a degree d irreducible plane curve other than the conic with multiplicities m_i, Bézout gives Σ m_i<=2d and genus gives Σ m_i(m_i−1)<=(d−1)(d−2), hence strict self-intersection >=d−2>=0 for d>=2. Only exceptional E_i, secants L_ij (-1), and Q (4−n) are negative. Distinct selected −1 curves must be disjoint, hence secant edges pairwise intersect and avoid selected exceptional labels. Such edge families are stars (with singleton multiplicities corrected) or triangles; T_m=1+m[(1+t)^{m−1}−1]−binom(m,2)t+binom(m,3)t³. With Q, Schur complement against selected E gives −(n−4)+|E|<0, equivalently m>=5. BFN converts support classification to chambers. Since −K=H+Q is big and Q²<=−3, Bauer–Schmitz theorem gives infinite volumes exactly for Q supports. Independently reconstructed n=6 boundary total 1898 with 648 Q supports and n=7 finite 4671, infinite 3396, total 8067. All-n follows from Bézout/genus/Schur and star-triangle arguments, not finite tests.
residual_risks: Volume convention is the anticanonical truncation of Bauer–Schmitz, not a claim about arbitrary alternative normalization.
Positions are distinct on a smooth conic, n>=7; n=6 is only an independent boundary check.

final_claim: For n>=7 distinct points on a smooth plane conic, all Zariski chambers have support polynomials F_n(t)=Σ_{m=0}^n binom(n,m)t^{n−m}T_m(t) when Q excluded and G_n(t)=tΣ_{m=5}^n binom(n,m)t^{n−m}T_m(t) when conic Q included, where T_m counts pairwise-intersecting edge families in K_m. The two families have finite and infinite anticanonically truncated volume respectively.
